# Cuberta

> A free 3D editor for Windows and macOS. Connect Claude, GPT or any MCP agent and it builds whole locations. Export to Unity, Unreal, Blender, Godot.

Cuberta is a free 3D editor for Windows and macOS. It exposes a Model Context Protocol
server, so an AI agent — Claude Code or any other MCP client — can build whole locations
inside it: road networks with junctions and sidewalks, buildings with facades and furnished
interiors, terrain, vegetation and lighting. Scenes export as GLB or FBX with textures for
Unity, Unreal Engine, Blender and Godot. There is no account, no trial and no subscription.

## Pages

- [Home](https://cuberta.com/): what Cuberta is, with the Astronomer’s House, a scene an agent built on its own
- [Features](https://cuberta.com/features/): what the agent builds and the editor around it
- [Gallery](https://cuberta.com/gallery/): renders of six scenes AI agents built in Cuberta — The Astronomer’s House, Lighthouse on the Cape, Winter Lodge, Neon Alley, Mars Outpost Ares-7, Temple in the Jungle
- [How it works](https://cuberta.com/how-it-works/): install, connect an agent, describe a place, export
- [Specs](https://cuberta.com/specs/): system requirements and download files
- [FAQ](https://cuberta.com/faq/): price, agents, export, offline use
- [Download](https://cuberta.com/download/): all builds for Windows and macOS
- [Blog](https://cuberta.com/blog/): guides on AI level design, engine pipelines and agent workflows

Available in English, Russian (/ru/), Simplified Chinese (/zh/) and Japanese (/ja/).

## Downloads

- Windows installer: https://dl.cuberta.com/1.0.2/Cuberta-Setup-1.0.2.exe (220 MB)
- Windows portable: https://dl.cuberta.com/1.0.2/Cuberta-1.0.2-portable.exe (220 MB)
- macOS Apple Silicon: https://dl.cuberta.com/1.0.1/Cuberta-1.0.1-arm64.dmg (265 MB)
- macOS Intel: https://dl.cuberta.com/1.0.1/Cuberta-1.0.1-x64.dmg (267 MB)

## Articles

- [AI City Generator: Roads First, Then Blocks, Then Buildings](https://cuberta.com/blog/ai-city-generator-for-games/): Generated cities look right from above and fall apart on foot. Road hierarchy, block sizes, frontage, junctions — the numbers that make a city read as a city.
- [Import a GLB Environment Into Unity and Make It Playable](https://cuberta.com/blog/ai-generated-environments-in-unity/): A generated GLB or FBX location lands in Unity in minutes. Making it playable takes import settings, colliders and lighting — here is the whole path.
- [Importing an AI-Generated Level into Unreal Engine 5](https://cuberta.com/blog/ai-generated-levels-in-unreal-engine-5/): You have a GLB of a whole district and a UE5 project. What to check on import: scale, Nanite, Lumen, collision, and why one big actor never streams.
- [AI Interior Design in 3D: Why a Room Is Harder Than a Street](https://cuberta.com/blog/ai-interior-design-3d/): A room you can walk through is a different product from a picture of one. The clearances, the furniture graph and the lighting that decide which you get.
- [AI Level Design Tools in 2026: What Each One Actually Does](https://cuberta.com/blog/ai-level-design-tools-2026/): Five kinds of AI tool touch level design, and only some of them design anything. What each category produces, where it stops, and how to choose.
- [Blender MCP: What It Does Well and Where It Runs Out](https://cuberta.com/blog/blender-mcp-alternative/): An honest look at driving Blender with an AI agent: where Blender MCP wins outright, where its abstraction level costs you, and how to split the work.
- [Claude Code for 3D Modeling: What Actually Transfers](https://cuberta.com/blog/claude-code-3d-modeling/): A terminal coding agent that builds 3D locations: how the connection works, the prompt that holds up, the verification loop, and where it fails.
- [Free Level Design Software: The Whole Stack in 2026](https://cuberta.com/blog/free-level-design-software/): Every stage of a 3D environment has a free option in 2026. Here is the stack, what each licence actually permits, and where the free tier stops.
- [GLB vs FBX: Which Format to Hand Your Game Engine](https://cuberta.com/blog/glb-vs-fbx-for-game-engines/): What glTF/GLB and FBX each actually carry, where each one quietly loses data, and which to hand Unity, Unreal, Godot, Blender and the web.
- [AI-Generated Levels in Godot: From GLB to a Real Scene](https://cuberta.com/blog/godot-ai-level-generation/): Import a generated location into Godot as GLB, then give it collision, occluders, lighting and a re-import path that does not throw away your work.
- [How to Build a 3D Village with an AI Agent, Pass by Pass](https://cuberta.com/blog/how-to-build-a-3d-village-with-ai/): From a blank scene to a walkable village in five passes: terrain, roads, plots, buildings, dressing — with the exact instructions to give an AI agent.
- [MCP Servers for 3D and Game Dev: Tool Design Is the Product](https://cuberta.com/blog/mcp-servers-for-3d-and-game-dev/): An MCP server that exposes run_python helps an agent with nothing. What separates a 3D tool surface an agent can actually use from one it cannot.
- [How to Optimize an AI-Generated 3D Scene for Games](https://cuberta.com/blog/optimize-ai-generated-scenes-for-games/): Generated locations fail differently from hand-built ones. Measure first, then fix materials, instancing, LODs, textures and culling in that order.
- [Procedural Generation vs AI Agents: Which One You Want](https://cuberta.com/blog/procedural-generation-vs-ai-agents/): Noise, grammars and WFC against an agent driving an editor. Determinism, scale, runtime and iteration cost — the axes that decide which one you need.
- [Text to 3D Scene: How One Prompt Becomes a Whole Location](https://cuberta.com/blog/text-to-3d-scene-generator/): Text-to-3D usually means one object at a time. Generating a whole scene — roads, buildings, terrain, light — is a different problem with different answers.

## FAQ

### Is Cuberta free?

Yes. Cuberta is free to download and use on Windows and macOS, with no account, no trial period and no subscription. The bundled models, materials and skies are included.

### Which AI agents work with Cuberta?

Any MCP client. Claude Code is the one most people start with, but the app exposes a standard Model Context Protocol server, so anything that speaks MCP can drive the scene. You bring your own agent and your own API access.

### What can the agent actually build?

Whole locations — road networks with junctions and sidewalks, blocks of buildings with real facades, terrain, vegetation, street furniture and lighting. It also builds single objects: a house with a furnished interior, a room, a prop. If you can describe it, it will attempt it.

### Which engines can I export to?

GLB and FBX come out with textures included, which covers Unity, Unreal Engine, Blender, Godot and anything else that reads glTF or FBX.

### Do I need to know 3D modeling?

No. You describe the place in plain language and correct the agent when it goes the wrong way. Knowing your engine's import settings helps more than knowing how to model.

### How is this different from Blender MCP?

Blender MCP hands an agent the whole of Blender, which is powerful and slow — the agent spends its turns writing Python against a general-purpose modeller. Cuberta is a purpose-built editor for locations: the tools it exposes are already about roads, buildings, terrain and placement, so the agent works at that level instead of rebuilding it every time.

### Does Cuberta work offline?

The editor and its bundled content run offline. The agent itself needs whatever connection your model provider requires, and signing in is only needed to browse your Wandy3D library.

### What are the system requirements?

64-bit Windows 10 or 11, or macOS on Apple Silicon or Intel. Any GPU from the last decade will do. The builds are not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Privacy & Security will ask you to confirm the first launch.

Frequently asked questions
==========================

Short answers here. The blog has the longer versions.

[Blog](/blog/)

Is Cuberta free?
----------------

Yes. Cuberta is free to download and use on Windows and macOS, with no account, no trial period and no subscription. The bundled models, materials and skies are included.

Which AI agents work with Cuberta?
----------------------------------

Any MCP client. Claude Code is the one most people start with, but the app exposes a standard Model Context Protocol server, so anything that speaks MCP can drive the scene. You bring your own agent and your own API access.

What can the agent actually build?
----------------------------------

Whole locations — road networks with junctions and sidewalks, blocks of buildings with real facades, terrain, vegetation, street furniture and lighting. It also builds single objects: a house with a furnished interior, a room, a prop. If you can describe it, it will attempt it.

Which engines can I export to?
------------------------------

GLB and FBX come out with textures included, which covers Unity, Unreal Engine, Blender, Godot and anything else that reads glTF or FBX.

Do I need to know 3D modeling?
------------------------------

No. You describe the place in plain language and correct the agent when it goes the wrong way. Knowing your engine's import settings helps more than knowing how to model.

How is this different from Blender MCP?
---------------------------------------

Blender MCP hands an agent the whole of Blender, which is powerful and slow — the agent spends its turns writing Python against a general-purpose modeller. Cuberta is a purpose-built editor for locations: the tools it exposes are already about roads, buildings, terrain and placement, so the agent works at that level instead of rebuilding it every time.

Does Cuberta work offline?
--------------------------

The editor and its bundled content run offline. The agent itself needs whatever connection your model provider requires, and signing in is only needed to browse your Wandy3D library.

What are the system requirements?
---------------------------------

64-bit Windows 10 or 11, or macOS on Apple Silicon or Intel. Any GPU from the last decade will do. The builds are not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Privacy & Security will ask you to confirm the first launch.

The short version

*   We collect what you give us (your account, your photos, prompts and models, your messages), what the Services record when you use them, and limited information from Google, Apple and payment providers.
*   We use it to run Wandy3D: to create your models, keep your library, process payments, keep the Services safe and improve them.
*   Your photos and prompts are stored with your models and are private to you. Our AI and cloud providers process them, including OpenAI, Anthropic, RunPod and Cloudflare.
*   By default, we may use your content to improve our AI. You can turn this off at any time in [Profile → Privacy](/profile#privacy).
*   We don't sell personal information, we don't show ads and we don't use advertising cookies.
*   You can see, correct, get a copy of and delete your data. You can delete your account yourself at [wandy3d.com/delete-account](/delete-account).

This Privacy Policy explains how **WORNOX GAMES - FZCO** ("Wandy3D", "we", "us" or "our") collects, uses, shares and protects personal information when you use Wandy3D. Wandy3D includes the website at wandy3d.com, our apps, and our API and integrations (together, the "Services"). We are the controller of your personal information. Wandy3D was previously called HiGen3D.

Terms used here have the meaning given in our [Terms of Service](/terms). If you use Wandy3D through an AI assistant or another app, section 16 explains what that app receives.

01Information we collect
------------------------

### 1.1 Account and profile

*   **When you sign in with Google:** your email address, name, profile picture and Google account ID.
*   **When you sign in with Apple (in our apps):** your Apple account ID, your email address (which may be a private relay address) and your name, if you share it.
*   **When you sign in with a code sent by email:** your email address. We keep it with your account so that the same address always opens the same account.
*   **Your profile:** the username you choose, your display name and avatar, and when you joined.

### 1.2 Your content

*   **Inputs:** the photos, drawings, reference and style images you upload, and the text you type: prompts, edit instructions, motion and expression descriptions and settings. When you create a model from a video, the frames are picked in your browser, and only the selected frames are uploaded, not the video.
*   **Photo metadata:** image files from phones and cameras often carry hidden information (EXIF and similar metadata), such as where and when a photo was taken and which device took it. When a photo or drawing you upload to create or edit a model reaches our servers, we remove that information before we process or store the image.
*   **Prepared images:** the images we make from your Inputs before 3D generation, for example a cleaned-up version of your photo with the background removed, and concept images drawn from a text prompt.
*   **Outputs:** your models and their versions, textures, rigs, motions, thumbnails, preview videos, exported, print and maker files, and model names and tags (we suggest them automatically).

### 1.3 Community and social features

*   What you publish: models, their names, descriptions and themes.
*   Your likes, saves, remixes and model views.
*   Your friends and friend requests.
*   Your direct messages, including models you send and when messages were sent.
*   Reports you send or that others send about your content.

### 1.4 Purchases

Your plan and its renewal status, credit balances and history, model unlocks, and transaction records (IDs, amounts, dates). For a plan or offer bought with a single payment: its status (active or refunded), your place in a limited offer, if it has one, and the dates of your monthly credit refills. Card details are handled by Stripe, Apple or Google; we never see your full card number. For the API: your top-ups, your API balance and its history (charges and refunds), the spending limits and alerts you set and, if you turn on auto-recharge, a reference to the card saved at Stripe (its brand, last four digits and expiry date).

### 1.5 Messages you send us

Support requests and feedback: your email address, the topic, your message and any attachments, linked to your account if you're signed in.

### 1.6 Notifications and preferences

Push tokens for your browsers and devices, your notification and email preferences, your language, and a log of the emails and notifications we send you. For emails, the log includes their delivery status: whether an email was delivered, opened, a link in it was clicked, it bounced or it was marked as spam.

### 1.7 Invitations and rewards

If you joined through an invitation, who invited you. We also record the rewards you receive, such as invitation credits, remix rewards and daily rewards.

### 1.8 Developer features

Your API keys and connections with AI assistants. For these, we store only a one-way hash of each key or token, together with the app's name and when it was last used. We also record the requests made through them. For calls made with your API keys we keep a log of the latest requests (time, method, path, status, duration and cost) for 14 days, to show it to you in the API platform and to investigate problems. If you use webhooks, we keep each key's signing secret (we need it to sign events) and, for 30 days, each job's callback URL and delivery status.

### 1.9 Usage and device information

*   **Product activity:** what you do in the Services, with your account ID and the time. For example: sign-ins, generations and their settings and results, publishing, likes and downloads, and the features you use.
*   **Website analytics:** we measure visits with our own analytics, without cookies. For each page view we record the page, language, referring website, campaign tags, country (derived from the IP address), device type and browser. We don't store your IP address for this. Instead, we compute a visitor code from your IP address and browser details using a secret that changes every day, so visits can't be linked across days. A session code is kept only in your browser tab. If you're signed in, the visit is linked to your account.
*   **Purchase steps:** events such as viewing the pricing page or starting a checkout, linked to your account or session.
*   **What you make models for:** right after you sign up we ask three short questions: what you make 3D models for (for example 3D printing, games, Roblox, a shop or AR, animation, design, or just for fun), what kind of objects, and how you work with 3D (just starting, for yourself, professionally or as a team). Accounts created earlier may instead have been asked one optional question after their first model. We keep the answers with your account to tailor tips and offers on the site and to understand who uses the Services and what to improve.
*   **Technical data:** IP address, browser and device type, operating system, app version, timestamps and error logs. We use these for security, rate limiting and troubleshooting.
*   **Our mobile apps:** Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics (Google) collect app usage statistics and crash reports.

### 1.10 The HiGen Motors game (closed)

HiGen Motors, our mobile game, is closed and can no longer be installed. If you played it, the game data saved with your account stays with it and is deleted when you delete your account: your garage and tuning settings, maps you created and published, races, leaderboard results, ratings and likes.

### 1.11 Information from others

We receive information from:

*   Google and Apple, when you sign in;
*   Stripe, Apple, Google and RevenueCat, about your purchases and subscriptions;
*   other users, when they invite you, share a model with you or report content.

### 1.12 Photos of people

Your Inputs may show people. We use them only to create the model you ask for. We don't use face recognition, we don't create biometric templates or identifiers, and we don't link people in your images to any account. Upload images of other people only if you have their permission. Please don't include sensitive information, such as health data or identity documents, in your Inputs.

### 1.13 Ad measurement

When you come to Wandy3D from one of our ads or from a link with campaign tags, we record which ad or campaign brought you. This shows us which ads bring people who sign up and pay, so we spend our advertising budget on what works.

*   **What we store:** the click identifier the ad platform added to the link (for example Google's gclid or Meta's fbclid), the campaign tags (utm\_source, utm\_medium, utm\_campaign, utm\_content, utm\_term), the page you landed on, the referring website, the time, your country and device type, together with the daily visitor code described in 1.9. When you create an account, we save where you came from as its first touch: the ad or campaign, or otherwise the referring website of your first visit that day. For accounts that came from an ad we also note the date of the sign-up and the date, product and amount of each purchase.
*   **In your browser:** outside the EEA, the UK and Switzerland, the click record is also kept in your browser tab (session storage) until you sign in or close the tab. In the EEA, the UK and Switzerland we don't keep anything in your browser for this.
*   **Ad platforms:** today we don't send this information to any ad platform. Before we start reporting sign-ups or purchases to the platform whose ad brought you (for example Google or Meta), we'll update this policy, and in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland we'll do it only with your consent.
*   **Retention:** click records that are not linked to an account are deleted after 90 days. The first touch of your account and the records of its sign-up and purchases kept for ad measurement are kept for 13 months, and deleted with your account.
*   **Never sold:** we don't sell this information and we don't use it to show you ads. In the EEA and the UK, our legal basis is our legitimate interest in measuring our own advertising.

### 1.14 3D files you bring to our tools

When you use our free tools — the [print check](/tools/print-check) and the [file converter](/tools/glb-to-stl) — with your own GLB, STL, OBJ or 3MF file, your browser turns an STL, OBJ or 3MF file into a GLB and sends us that GLB (a GLB file is sent as it is), with the file's name, size and triangle count. We use it only to run the tool you asked for and to show you its result again. It is stored privately, processed on our cloud servers, and deleted automatically 29 days after the upload together with everything made from it — or right away when you delete it or your account. Uploaded 3D files are never used to train or improve AI, whatever your AI-improvement setting, and they never become models, library items or Community posts. Conversions to STL, 3MF and GLB are made in your browser, and nothing is uploaded for them. The same rules apply to a 3D file you upload on our craft maker pages ([papercraft](/papercraft-maker), [laser-cut layers](/laser-cut-layers), [brick sets](/brick-set-maker)): we open and measure it once on our own server before it is stored, and then use it only to build the craft files you ask for.

### 1.15 Live face and the phone camera

**Live face** lets your face move an animated model through your device's camera. The camera picture is processed in your browser, on your device: we don't receive, upload or store it. Face tracking turns each camera frame into numbers that describe your expression (for example, how far your mouth is open) and the turn of your head, and these numbers move the model on your screen. Clips and videos you record stay in your browser tab until you download them, and the microphone is used only when you turn on sound for a video or record your voice for the model to speak. A video file or a sound file you choose to move the model is read the same way, in your browser: we don't receive, upload or store it, and the lip movements are worked out from the sound on your device. A text you type for the model to say is turned into speech in your browser too: we don't receive, upload or store the text, and the voice files your browser downloads from our server for this are the same for everyone. With the **phone camera**, your phone does the face tracking and sends only these numbers to your computer, never the picture: directly between the two devices when they can reach each other, otherwise through our server, which passes them on as they arrive and doesn't store or log them. To connect the two devices directly, each one asks our server which internet address it is seen from, and the two exchange these addresses through our server; we don't store or log them. We don't use any of this to recognise or identify you, and we don't create biometric templates.

**Saved recordings.** A recording stays only in your browser tab until you press **Save** on it. Then we store its motion — the numbers that move the model, never a picture — and, if you leave sound on, its sound, together with that model in your account. A saved recording is deleted when you delete it or your account, and together with the model's files when you delete the model. Other people see it only if you share its link, and only if they can already open that model — through a link to the model or in the Community.

02How we use information
------------------------

*   **To provide the Services:** create and manage your account; create models from your Inputs; keep your library and versions; run features such as editing, retexturing, remeshing, rigging, motions, parts, style kits, exports, 3D print and maker files, AR and sharing.
*   **To handle payments:** plans, credits, model unlocks, rewards and invitations. This includes preventing abuse of free credits, for example one person opening many accounts.
*   **To run the Community and social features:** show what you publish, credit remixes, connect friends and deliver messages. We also recommend models based on activity such as views, likes and generations.
*   **To communicate with you:** service messages (for example, that a model is ready, or about your account, security and billing) and replies to support requests. We send marketing emails, such as offers, only if you haven't turned them off, and every one has a one-click unsubscribe link. Push notifications only if you allow them.
*   **To keep the Services safe:** moderate content, enforce our Terms and Acceptable Use Policy, prevent fraud, spam, abuse and security incidents, and apply rate limits.
*   **To improve the Services:** analyse usage, fix problems, check quality and develop new features.
*   **To improve our AI:** see section 3. This is on by default, and you can turn it off.
*   **To comply with the law:** respond to lawful requests, establish or defend legal claims and keep the records the law requires.

We don't make decisions that have legal or similarly significant effects on you based solely on automated processing. Automated tools help us moderate content and prevent abuse, and a person reviews any decision you contest.

03Improving our AI
------------------

Wandy3D gets better when our own AI models learn from real use. Unless you turn this off, we may use the following to train, test and evaluate our models, for example our photo preparation, 3D generation and texturing models:

*   your Inputs (photos, drawings, prompts and instructions);
*   the images we prepare from your Inputs;
*   your Outputs;
*   related technical details, such as the settings used and which version you kept.

We keep copies for this purpose in a separate dataset with restricted access.

*   **What we never use:** your name, email address, messages, support requests or payment details. We don't sell or publish these datasets.
*   **Your choice:** this is on by default, on free and paid plans. We ask you after you sign up, and you can turn it off at any time in [Profile → Privacy](/profile#privacy). When you turn it off, we stop adding your content and delete the copies we kept for this purpose, normally within 30 days. Models already trained on earlier content can't be untrained.
*   **Requests made with an API key** are never used to improve our AI, whatever this setting says.
*   **Legal basis (EEA and UK):** our legitimate interest in improving the Services. Turning the setting off is how you object, and we then stop.
*   **Our AI providers** process your content only to provide their services to us (see section 5).

04Legal bases (EEA and UK)
--------------------------

If you are in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom or Switzerland, we rely on these legal bases:

| Purpose | Information | Legal basis |

| Providing the Services: account, generation, library, Community, messages, payments, support and service messages | Account, content, purchase, communication and technical data | Performance of our contract with you |
| Safety, fraud and abuse prevention, moderation, analytics, product improvement, recommendations and improving our AI | Usage, technical and content data | Our legitimate interests in a safe, working and improving service. You can object at any time |
| Marketing emails about Wandy3D | Email address and preferences | Legitimate interests (offers similar to what you use, with an opt-out in every email), or consent where the law requires it |
| Push notifications | Device and browser tokens | Consent, given through your browser or device permission. You can withdraw it at any time |
| Tax, accounting and lawful requests | Purchase and account data | Legal obligation |

05How we share information
--------------------------

### 5.1 Service providers

These providers process information on our behalf, under contracts that limit their use of it to providing their services to us:

| Provider | What they do for us | Information they receive |

| OpenAI (USA) | They prepare drawings for 3D generation (clean-up, cut-out). They draw concept images for text-to-3D, edits by prompt and style kits. When Anthropic's service is unavailable, they do its tasks instead (model names, descriptions and search tags, rigging options, style-kit item names, motion translations, expression clips) | Your drawings, reference images (including the photo of a model you edit by prompt), prompts and instructions; when they stand in for Anthropic, the same data Anthropic gets |
| Anthropic (USA) | They describe each new model from its picture: a name, description and search tags, what the object is (its category, style, typical real-world size and whether it has hair or fur, which guides how we build it) and flags for our moderation. They also suggest rigging options, name the items of style kits, translate motion descriptions and turn a description of facial expressions into an expression clip (we don't store that description). They are never asked to identify people | Small copies of your photos, drawings and the pictures generated for your models, preview images of your models; your text prompts (as context), style-kit prompts, motion descriptions and descriptions of facial expressions |
| RunPod (USA; data centres worldwide) | Photo preparation for 3D generation (clean-up, cut-out), 3D generation and processing on GPU and CPU servers | Your photos, prepared images, model files and motion descriptions |

## Cuberta: facts from cuberta.com and wandy3d.com

**Pages read:** https://cuberta.com/, https://wandy3d.com/cuberta, https://cuberta.com/llms.txt, https://cuberta.com/specs/, https://cuberta.com/faq/, https://cuberta.com/how-it-works/, https://wandy3d.com/privacy (last updated November 18, 2026), https://wandy3d.com/terms (last updated November 12, 2026). Nothing was downloaded or signed up for. The current version is 1.0.2 for Windows and 1.0.1 for macOS (https://cuberta.com/specs/).

### MCP and agents
- Cuberta "exposes a Model Context Protocol server" and "anything that speaks MCP can drive the scene" (https://cuberta.com/llms.txt, https://cuberta.com/faq/). Claude Code is the usual start, and GPT or any MCP client also works (https://wandy3d.com/cuberta).
- Setup: install, open Cuberta, press "Copy connect command" in the top right, and paste it into the terminal where your agent runs (https://cuberta.com/how-it-works/). The actual command text is not stated.
- You bring your own agent and model access (https://cuberta.com/specs/).
- **Not stated:** the MCP tool names, parameters, or any tool-reference docs page. The site's llms.txt and nav list no docs page. Blog posts that may describe the tool surface were not fetched: https://cuberta.com/blog/mcp-servers-for-3d-and-game-dev/ and https://cuberta.com/blog/claude-code-3d-modeling/.

### Platform and headless use
- Windows: 64-bit Windows 10 or 11, installer or portable build. macOS: Apple Silicon or Intel. Any GPU from the last decade (https://cuberta.com/specs/).
- **Linux is not listed as supported.**
- The site describes a desktop app with a viewport and says the agent's work "appears in the viewport as it happens" (https://cuberta.com/). Headless operation is **not stated**.
- Editor and bundled content work offline. The agent needs its own model connection (https://cuberta.com/faq/).
- Builds are not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen or macOS will ask for confirmation on first launch (https://cuberta.com/specs/).

### Geometry
- Stated: road networks with junctions and sidewalks, building blocks with facades, furnished interiors, single rooms or props, terrain, vegetation, street furniture, and lighting and sky (https://cuberta.com/faq/, https://cuberta.com/features/ as linked from https://cuberta.com/).
- Stated: "Hills, vegetation, sky and the time of day" (https://cuberta.com/).
- **Not stated:** curved tubes or tunnels, arbitrary custom meshes built by the agent, and whether roads and buildings are procedurally generated.

### Importing images and meshes
- Wandy3D library and community models can be dragged into the scene (https://wandy3d.com/cuberta).
- Turning a photo into a 3D model inside Cuberta is stated. It runs on Wandy3D and uses credits (https://wandy3d.com/cuberta).
- **Not stated:** importing a reference image or a GLB, OBJ, or FBX file from disk.

### Textures and materials
- Bundled models, materials and skies are included (https://cuberta.com/faq/).
- Exports include textures (https://cuberta.com/specs/).
- **Not stated:** applying your own image texture to geometry.

### Export
- GLB and FBX, with textures included (https://cuberta.com/specs/).
- Unity: FBX imports as-is. GLB needs the glTFast package. Unreal: FBX imports as-is. GLB uses the built-in glTF importer. Godot: GLB is preferred. Blender: File → Import → glTF 2.0 or FBX (https://cuberta.com/how-it-works/).
- **Not stated:** OBJ export.

### Pricing and limits
- Cuberta is free: "no account, no trial, no subscription" (https://cuberta.com/faq/, https://cuberta.com/specs/).
- Sign-in with Wandy3D is optional, needed only to browse your library and community models (https://cuberta.com/specs/).
- Generating models in Cuberta costs Wandy3D credits (https://wandy3d.com/cuberta).
- Downloads are free inside Cuberta, even on the free plan. On wandy3d.com, downloads require PRO (https://wandy3d.com/cuberta).
- **Not stated:** any scene size, polygon, or usage limits in Cuberta. Agent usage is billed to your own model provider.

### Privacy
- **There is no Cuberta-specific privacy policy in what I read.** The Wandy3D policy at https://wandy3d.com/privacy describes its "Services" as the website, "our apps, and our API and integrations". It does not name Cuberta.
- Section 16 covers AI assistants connected to a Wandy3D account. A connected assistant "receives only what its requests return". Models an assistant makes are processed "like an upload on the website".
- Generation uses subprocessors including OpenAI, Anthropic, RunPod, Cloudflare, and Contabo (section 5.1).
- AI-improvement training is **on by default** for uploaded inputs, prompts, and outputs. It applies to free and paid plans. You can turn it off in Profile → Privacy. Requests made with an API key are never used for training.
- Retention for models and inputs: until deleted, and files are erased within 30 days of deletion.
- **Not stated:** whether a scene you build locally in the desktop editor is uploaded or stored. Also not stated: whether any local-only data leaves the machine.

### Terms and ownership
- Terms: https://wandy3d.com/terms.
- Paid Outputs, meaning outputs created on an active paid plan or with a model unlock, "belong to you". They may be used "in games, apps, films, ads, renders, prints and products for sale" (section 4.2).
- Free Outputs "belong to Wandy3D". You get a personal, non-commercial licence (section 4.2).
- Section 3.3 says downloading or exporting model files "requires an active paid plan or a model unlock". This conflicts with the Cuberta claim that downloads are free on the free plan. Section 3.3 also says "maker files" do not need a plan. The terms do not say how this applies to Cuberta.
- **Not stated:** whether a scene the agent builds in Cuberta from primitives or procedural geometry counts as a Wandy3D "Output". This determines whether commercial game use is covered, so it needs a direct answer from the vendor.
- AI outputs "may not be protected by copyright" in every country, and no warranty is given (section 4.2, section 15).

### Other links on the sites
- Blog articles on Unity, Unreal, Godot, and GLB vs FBX are linked from https://cuberta.com/how-it-works/ and https://cuberta.com/llms.txt. I did not fetch them.
- https://wandy3d.com/support, https://wandy3d.com/acceptable-use, and https://wandy3d.com/developers are linked from the Wandy3D pages. I did not fetch them.
